title: I build this in under 10 minutes and now I wonder where the fun went.
author: DearObjective4053
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/hnej6794dt2i1.png

So with fable 5.2 you can do all these amazing things. Like create a infinite-multiplayer-doodle-game-world in minutes. So I just build this: [https://doodleton.pages.dev/](https://doodleton.pages.dev/)

Now I sometimes wonder, where did the fun go? The work you have to put in to vibecode something into existence. Instead of having something up and running in minutes. And someone can steal / copy the thing you just made in even less time.

Is this something you guys experience as well? The part where vibecoding stuff goes 'too fast'? I mean we can build unlimited awesome things, and we need to challenge ourselves to make cool things. But sometimes I miss the joy of building small things and that is was actually hard to build those things.

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body:
It goes too slow imo

Everybody is saying it's so fast yet to make a real game you need to work on it for months still.

replies.author: DearObjective4053
replies.body: You'd expect AI to also do things like game mechanics / making it fun and repeatable already you mean?

replies.author: No_Background9234
replies.body: AI is just a glorified yes man, it will only go as far as you ask it too

replies.author: PositiveScarcity8909
replies.body: Even using AI there are plenty of challenges ahead of you.

comments.author: OrcasareDolphins
comments.body: But this isn’t even fun for more than a couple of minutes. Making a game fun is more than just a few prompts. Making a good game still takes months, creativity, and an understanding of what makes a game actually fun.

replies.author: DearObjective4053
replies.body: okay well this example isn't a fun game no. Maybe it's just the first rough draft that's super quick. I just enjoyed the creation of a rough draft being hard work too if you know what I mean.

replies.author: DearObjective4053
replies.body:
Going back and forth, thinking of solutions / work arounds etc. 

I come from an animation background and I found it hard to make stuff work before (AI assisted).

replies.author: Aeweisafemalesheep
replies.body:
"Going back and forth, thinking of solutions / work arounds etc." what does that mean?  

Like there are challenges with design  

Code  

Blender  

Whatever, like tools and editors and code stuff.  

Sure, we see that something can throw stuff out but i've been looking at a ton of stuff that's been posted lately and the only things that have it together are made by like 20 year industry veterans or long time modders that day job in a similar industry. So they strong point a skill set or two and minor in 2-3 others and have worked specific IPs or genres and their ai stuff is essentially doing stuff that feels like file clerk bullshit or something they'd give to a Jr who has no real control.   

Everyone else seems to be near the "do it for me" and then it's just like mario cart, a generic art style, and a theme or mechanic from another game like fzero which is what a 2nd or 3rd year should spend a lot of time on. Like in the racing or liminal driving games space, over the last 10 years, i've seen a ton of junk that kinda looks cool for a few dollars on steam or someone makes a decent [itch.io](http://itch.io) game jam/prototype.  

If we know what we want because we have taste and exp and a mind to design, then we should be able to prototype something that moves the real art forward now instead of spending 6 months making bare bones. Like, i don't need a full band/orchestra, i have keyboards, a singer and guitar plus hairspray to make a goth band. But you still need to understand music, and i'm seeing that a lot of people have no fucking taste. Ya know? Like the open mic guy who covers brown eyed girl.

replies.author: DearObjective4053
replies.body:
Yes this is perfect. This is very well described thank you. 

Sometimes it looks like it's blending all together, but it's really not and I do feel the same that the most awesome stuff comes from the veterans.

replies.author: Aeweisafemalesheep
replies.body:
The problem is at the highest, macro scale, an issue of the design of the technology.

Given ai crap only spits out stuff that has been done before. Like we have 3 sets of 25 numbers. Set A \[1....25\], Set B\[1....25\] and so on.

And say games are typically an element of each set ordered.

So like Get a random element from A,B, and C.

We've got like over 10,000 combos, ez, here.

So some game is like 3,22,14

Okay, if we have steams market and most games are a set of those numbers

Which are the most common numbers or groupings that we see?

Which groupings frequently result in junk tier games from a formal/mechanical design perspective?

Art design perspective?

And so on.

So anyone who is not in the know might happen to have an uncommon number generated for them like say 18,24,25 or something?

Whatever,

It's just the least likely and it kinda works but doesnt.

That might get crowned as new or innovative when 3,7, and new element \*\*26\*\*,   a new element in a set, would actually be something new.

And it will take design plus someone who has classic code skill to make a new element for a set and perhaps some friends to help with other things there. Or at least that's my current bet. But don't mistake numbers of the set that dont happen too often for something completely original.

So i think i've made my fuzzy point well enough.

People gotta play stuff, get good at stuff where getting good is required, and also try to accurately model shit (edit: accuracy could be terintino or john wick or mr fox levels of style because thats accurate fantasy bros, fuck you).    And so far everyones panning for gold when they shouldve learned the alchemy that goes into the chemistry to make TNT and blow up a fucking mountain side.

comments.author: Shleepy1
comments.body: I don’t use fable and mostly sonnet. I make all the decisions and the process is rather slow with a lot of playtesting and iterations. My project is rather simple though (a shmup). Fun was the greatest in the beginning, for the first month. Second month feels much more like a chore but it really improves. Classic pareto principle: 80% done in 20% of the dev time. The last 20% polishing take 80% now

comments.author: viral-architect
comments.body: Slow and janky. The erase button doesn't seem to erase ponds. How will it scale with 500 active users?

replies.author: DearObjective4053
replies.body: oh yes Im sure I can get it to. My point was that you can go for something simple so fast now, that sometimes I miss the challenge of creating something.

replies.author: Tiamitsu
replies.body: Okay, I understand what you mean, but personally I just find it helps to put an idea on paper more quickly, and I really like that. I've been a 2D artist, animator, and also a video game modeler, but I've always loved sketching more than anything else because I really enjoyed just getting ideas out of my head quickly. I think AI is really cool for that. For me, I feel more like an art director in this case, and I like that.

replies.author: viral-architect
replies.body: No hate, just keep working on it. You are right.

comments.author: Andress1
comments.body: The fun is enjoying what you created not creating it

comments.author: teejayaiartdirector
comments.body: You iterate on ideas fast with building game prototypes fast and to test them and vouch if that game is worth going further with, if you're creative and make many games you can play many games, make games you always wanted as a kid and so on. The fun is still there but it's different. 🤔 **Building fast is part of the fun!**🔥

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body: you can always learn how to code the normal way if its too fast for you.

comments.author: Tiamitsu
comments.body: It's not well optimized it lags terribly on my end. Otherwise, I don't really understand what this game is about. Do we just draw things, like houses, and place them wherever we want? There's no tutorial, nothing. I mean, there's practically no gameplay other than just placing things in a setting? You can create small, quick things and prototype ideas with the AI, but making a complete, optimized, playable, and fun game still requires work and time, depending on the complexity of the project.

replies.author: DearObjective4053
replies.body:
yeah this is just a protoype / few-shotted thing-y. 

My point was that the fun in building stuff sometimes disappears for me, because some things can be done fast. But maybe it just applies on prototypes and quick builds instead of the real thing, right. I'm unsure, I sometimes miss the time where everything you made took time.

replies.author: Tiamitsu
replies.body: Yes, I understand, I felt that way a bit at first, but when you realize the freedom it gives you to create and develop projects wherever you want, it's really cool. And believe me, it does take time, haha. I've been working on my project for almost a month, 8 to 10 hours a day, and I'm still far from finished.

replies.author: DearObjective4053
replies.body:
You have a link of what you are building? :) 

Maybe it's also because I'm creating a lot of smaller things lately, have to find a bigger project to create. I mean I still love to create, it's just a feeling that sometimes pops up.

replies.author: Tiamitsu
replies.body: I don't have a link, I haven't shared it yet. I'm working on a god game, a life simulation like The Sims. The systems in there are very large, it requires a lot of iterative work, and on top of that, I'm doing 3D pixel art, so that's quite demanding too. But I'll be posting images and videos soo, I just need to finish a few more systems that are important in the game :-) But indeed, since you seem to have experimented with some systems, you could start a real project and see where it leads you.
